ColonyCouncil.DilemmaDef.label: a guest who wants to stay

texts.li: {X_nameDef} came with the {FACTION} guests to rest a few days, and has spent most of them with {A_nameDef}: at the workbench, at supper, out on the wall at dusk. Now {X_nameDef} has asked the council whether a guest can stop being a guest.\n\n{FACTION} won't be glad to lose {X_objective}. {A_nameDef} has been very careful not to look at the council while it's discussed.

"I haven't felt this much at home in years." On the last night of the visit, {X_nameDef} came to the council with {X_possessive} pack still unpacked and asked to stay, and said it was {A_nameDef}, most of all, who had made it so.\n\n{A_nameDef} has offered to share {A_possessive} rations until {X_nameDef} finds {X_possessive} feet.

[x:roomgood] {X_nameDef} has stayed in the guest room three nights running and says it's the best bed {X_pronoun} has slept in since leaving home. Tonight {X_pronoun} asked {A_nameDef}, in front of the council, whether {X_pronoun} could keep the room for good.\n\nThe rest of the {FACTION} party have stopped speaking to {X_objective}. {A_nameDef} has already said yes, though it isn't {A_possessive} answer to give.

[winter] The {FACTION} guests leave tomorrow, into the snow, and {X_nameDef} doesn't want to go with them. Every morning of the visit {X_nameDef} has split wood for the colony without being asked. {A_nameDef} says that's the sort of person you keep.

li.label: Take {X_nameDef} in
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} moved {X_possessive} things out of the guest room and into the colony that same night. The rest of the {FACTION} party went on without {X_objective}, and their goodbyes were short.

li.label: Take {X_objective} in, with a gift to {FACTION}
li.outcome: A hundred and fifty silver went out to the {FACTION} party at the gate with the council's thanks, and {X_nameDef} stayed behind. The parting was warmer than anyone expected.

li.label: Ask {X_objective} to come back another season
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} will be welcome another season, but not this time. {X_nameDef} took it well. {A_nameDef} walked {X_objective} out past the fields and came back quiet.

li.label: No
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} nodded at the answer, went back to the guest room, and didn't come out for supper.

texts.li: The food, the bed, the hammering from the workshop at dawn: {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has been through all of it with {A_nameDef}, at length. {X_nameDef} wants to know what the colony means to do about it before {X_pronoun} tells everyone on the road.

[x:roompoor|x:nobed] {X_nameDef} paid for a bed and got a cold corner, by {X_possessive} account, and this morning caught {A_nameDef} by the sleeve to ask for the silver back.\n\n{FACTION} are neighbors the colony would like to keep.

{X_nameDef} has been miserable since {X_pronoun} arrived, and has decided it's the colony's fault. This morning {X_pronoun} told {A_nameDef} that {FACTION} will hear what kind of welcome this place gives.

li.label: Give back the fee, and a good meal
li.outcome: {X_nameDef}'s silver was counted back into {X_possessive} hand, and the kitchen sent out the best plate it could manage. {X_nameDef} ate every bite and allowed that the place had its good points.

li.label: Have our best talker smooth it over
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} spent an hour with {X_nameDef}, listening more than talking. By the end {X_nameDef} was laughing at {X_possessive} own complaints.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} tried, but {X_nameDef} heard every soothing word as another insult, and is angrier than before.

li.label: They can take it or leave it
li.outcome: "This isn't an inn on the high road," {A_nameDef} told {X_nameDef}. {X_nameDef} went off muttering, and {A_nameDef} was left to hear the rest of it.
